desc: Implement `solve_cover(L, R)` using a greedy strategy (sort intervals by start, pick max end).
Implement coordinate compression for $R$ values to use in Fenwick tree.
Implement Fenwick tree to support `update(pos, val)` (max) and `query(pos)` (max).
Calculate `ans1`: min cost using exactly one Op 2 (iterate $i$, cost $1 + \text{solve\_cover}(L_i, R_i)$).
Calculate `ans2`: min cost using exactly two Op 2s.
Check for contained pairs ($j \subseteq i$): cost $2 + \text{solve\_cover}(L_j, R_j)$. Use Fenwick tree to find min `solve_cover` for $j$ with $L_j \ge L_i, R_j \le R_i$.
Check for partial overlaps ($L_j \ge L_i, R_j > R_i$): cost $2 + \text{solve\_cover}(L_j, R_i)$. Find $j$ with max $L_j$.
Calculate `ans3`: min cost using exactly one Op 1 (check if any interval covers $[1, N]$).
Determine global minimum and reconstruct the operation sequence.
